title: Blue box opt-out and Cambridge truck diversion
subtitle: Lancaster Street reconstruction, economic development funding, climate partnerships, Waterloo landfill station contract, roundabouts, Elmira transit and Stage 2 ION.
overview: The Planning and Works Committee recommended that the Region opt out of administering blue box service on March 2, 2024, leaving producers responsible for collection and processing until transition ends on December 31, 2025 {{vote:m10}}. Staff said residents will not notice changes until 2025, and the current system stays in place until then.

On the Cambridge truck diversion study, the committee sent the report back to staff for changes, including looking at no heavy trucks on Concession Street and a full noise wall along McQueen Shaver Boulevard. It is due at Council on August 30, 2023 {{vote:m9}}. The committee also recommended the Lancaster Street reconstruction design in Kitchener, which includes reserved bike lanes and removes some parking {{vote:m7}}.

The committee recommended an extra $500,000 a year for the Waterloo Region Economic Development Corporation from 2024, extensions of two collaborative climate funding agreements, and an $11.96 million consulting contract for the Waterloo Landfill transfer station renewal. A motion to reopen the Stage 2 ION project alternatives was defeated {{vote:m13}}; the ION report was received for information. The consent agenda also covered expropriations for two roundabouts, two more roundabout designs and an extension of Elmira local transit.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that the Region opt out of administering blue box service from March 2, 2024, and that staff extend contracts for collection of sources not covered by the new regulation until the end of transition.
The committee referred the report back to staff for changes discussed at the meeting, to return to Council on August 30, 2023.
The committee recommended the design concept for Lancaster Street from Wellington Street to Bridgeport Road, with reserved bike lanes and parking changes.
The committee recommended approving in principle the renewed WREDC partnership agreement and adding $500,000 a year in tax-levy funding from 2024, subject to budget approval.
The committee recommended extending the collaborative funding agreement with Cambridge, Kitchener and Waterloo for five years, at a total contribution of $315,380.
The committee recommended a four-year extension of the collaborative funding agreement with municipal and utility partners, at a total contribution of $358,768.
The committee recommended awarding HDR Corporation the detailed design and construction services contract for $11,958,177 plus taxes.
The committee defeated a motion to waive notice requirements for reconsidering the direction on three project alternatives in the Stage 2 ION business case.
